grounding.query: redis master OOMKilled 512Mi ConnectionError celery-worker checkout-svc 503
grounding.answer: The sources indicate that the Redis instance was out of memory and killed by the OOM killer, as evidenced by the log entry "Out of memory: Killed process 15366 (redis-server) total-vm:19497288kB, anon-rss:12311880kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB, UID:100 pgtables:35296kB oom_score_adj:0". For Celery tasks encountering connection errors with Redis, the sources suggest a timeout issue when running long-duration tasks, and a specific error "OOM command not allowed when used memory > ‘maxmemory’" indicates Redis has exceeded its memory limit. To address these issues, the sources recommend configuring Redis with appropriate `maxmemory` settings and ensuring sufficient system resources.

results.snippet:
The memory in VM 16GB  
Any suggestion would be usefull

Hello,

and welcome to this community forum. There has been some recent discussions around general memory usage during scans (including Redis related topics), i’m adding them below as a reference:

The solution was:

`# Size of SWAP
vm.overcommit_ratio = 25
vm.overcommit_memory = 1`

The Redis uses SWAP but if you disable the overcommit\_memory oom\_killer will be kill redis when the memory usage going crazy.

This was too early…  
The situationis:

All right I think this is solved.

reasoning.root_cause_analysis: Redis master pod OOMKilled after exceeding 512Mi memory limit, triggering downstream connection failures in celery workers, checkout-svc, and api-gateway.
remediation_plan: Increase Redis memory limit beyond current workload requirements
Configure Redis maxmemory and maxmemory-policy in configuration
Adjust VM overcommit settings (vm.overcommit_memory=1) if applicable
Scale Redis deployment or implement clustering to distribute load
Implement resource monitoring and alerting for memory utilization
Restart affected pods and verify service reconnection
reasoning.fix_recommendation: Configure Redis with appropriate maxmemory limit and policy, and ensure underlying node resources/overcommit settings prevent OOMKills.
